Let me think about the right logical relation for this calculus.

We have a two-run relation (relating terms from two executions). The context C is shared, so the relation must be compatible with a common typing context.

Standard approach (e.g., from "A Logical Relation for Monadic Encapsulation of State"? no). For noninterference in STLC with labels, a simple technique: interpret types as relations on *values*, parameterized by an "observer level" ℓ ∈ {Low, High}:

V(ℓ, Ty_Unit k) = {(v1,v2) | True} maybe with erase equality when k.reader ⊑ ℓ.
V(ℓ, Ty_Sum T1 T2 k) = if k.reader ⊑ ℓ then {(inl v1, inl v2) | (v1,v2) ∈ V(ℓ,T1)} ∪ {(inr...)} else True.
V(ℓ, Ty_Prod T1 T2 k) = if k.reader ⊑ ℓ then pairs with components related else True.
V(ℓ, Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k) = if k.reader ⊑ ℓ then { (f1,f2) | for all v1 v2, (v1,v2) ∈ V(ℓ,T1) -> applications related ... } else True.

Hmm, but the "protection" mechanism complicates: applications produce protected results with join of indirect_reader.

Alternative: interpret at an observer level that's fixed to Low (the attacker is Low). If a value's type has reader High, the attacker learns nothing: any two values related. If reader Low, the attacker sees the structure: relate structurally.

But then the indirect_reader is used to ensure that when a computation's result is protected, the attacker can't see it. The typing rules set the result security = ty_protect kappa.indirect_reader T. Approach A: "value interpretation at observer level ℓ, with type security determining observability".

Define for each type T and label ℓ (observer level), a relation on values:
```
VR ℓ T v1 v2 :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k => observability k ℓ -> erase_security v1 = erase_security v2   (* but units always erase to unit public; still fine *)
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k => if observable k ℓ then (exists w1 w2, v1 = inl w1 /\ v2 = inl w2 /\ VR ℓ T1 w1 w2) \/ (exists, inr) else True
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k => if observable k ℓ then exists w1 w1' w2 w2', v1 = pair w1 w2 /\ v2 = pair w1' w2' /\ VR ℓ T1 w1 w1' /\ VR ℓ T2 w2 w2' else True
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k => if observable k ℓ then forall a1 a2, VR ℓ T1 a1 a2 -> ... else True
  end
```
where `observable k ℓ := flows_to k.reader ℓ`.

```
Fixpoint VR (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | ... => ... VR T1 ... (recursive calls on subterms)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k => forall a1 a2 r, flows_to k.reader r -> R T1 a1 a2 -> R (ty_protect k.indirect_reader T2) (tm_app v1 a1 r) (tm_app v2 a2 r)
  end
with R (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, multi t1 v1 -> multi t2 v2 -> value v1 -> value v2 -> VR T v1 v2.
```

So:
```
Definition obs_security (kappa : security) : Prop := flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) Low.
Fixpoint R T t1 t2 :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k => flows_to k.indirect Low -> forall v1 v2, multi t1 v1 -> multi t2 v2 -> value v1 -> value v2 ->
      (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inl w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl w2 k2 /\ R T1 w1 w2) \/
      (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inr w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr w2 k2 /\ R T2 w1 w2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k => flows_to k.indirect Low -> forall v1 v2, ... ->
      exists k1 k2 a1 b1 a2 b2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\ R T1 a1 a2 /\ R T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k => flows_to k.indirect Low -> forall a1 a2 r, flows_to k.reader r -> R T1 a1 a2 ->
      Rprot k.indirect T2 (tm_app t1 a1 r) (tm_app t2 a2 r)
  end
with Rprot p T t1 t2 :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k => flows_to (join k.indirect p) Low -> forall v1 v2, ... -> (inl with R T1... ) \/ (inr with R T2 ...)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k => flows_to (join k.indirect p) Low -> ... R T1 ... /\ R T2 ...
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k => flows_to (join k.indirect p) Low -> forall a1 a2 r, flows_to (join k.reader p) r -> R T1 a1 a2 ->
      Rprot (join k.indirect p) T2 (app t1 a1 r) (app t2 a2 r)
  end.
```

```
Definition obs (p : label) (k : security) : Prop := flows_to (join k.(indirect_reader) p) Low.

Fixpoint R2 (T : ty) (p : label) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  lc_at 0 t1 /\ lc_at 0 t2 /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      obs p k -> forall v1 v2, multi t1 v1 -> multi t2 v2 -> value v1 -> value v2 ->
        (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inl w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl w2 k2 /\ R2 T1 Low w1 w2) \/
        (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inr w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr w2 k2 /\ R2 T2 Low w1 w2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      obs p k -> forall v1 v2, multi t1 v1 -> multi t2 v2 -> value v1 -> value v2 ->
        exists k1 k2 a1 b1 a2 b2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\ R2 T1 Low a1 a2 /\ R2 T2 Low b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      obs p k -> forall a1 a2 r, flows_to (join k.(reader) p) r -> R2 T1 Low a1 a2 ->
        R2 T2 (join p k.(indirect_reader)) (tm_app t1 a1 r) (tm_app t2 a2 r)
  end.
Definition R (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) := R2 T Low t1 t2.
```

Now, what about the T_Sub case with the strengthened unit clause and annotation bounds? Need monotonicity. Let's write the monotonicity statement carefully. We have R2 T p t1 t2 (the relation at T with top protection p). Subtyping T U relates the underlying types. But the protection parameter p acts on the top security: subtype T U with security_le k_T k_U should give R2 T p ⊆ R2 U p' when flows_to p p'. So:

`R2_mono: forall T U, subtype T U -> forall p q, flows_to p q -> forall t1 t2, R2 T p t1 t2 -> R2 U q t1 t2`.

Proven by induction on the subtype derivation. Let's check the cases:
- S_Unit k1 k2: goal R2 (Ty_Unit k1) p → R2 (Ty_Unit k2) q: both = lc ∧ True-clause; the unit clause under obs: R2 unit's structural clause requires evaluated values to be units; that's independent of annotations ✓.
- S_Sum T1 U1 T2 U2 k1 k2 (subtype T1 U1, subtype T2 U2, security_le k1 k2):
  Goal R2 (Sum T1 T2 k1) p t1 t2 → R2 (Sum U1 U2 k2) q t1 t2. Unfold: lc ✓; obs_q: flows_to (join k2.ind q) Low → need obs_p: flows_to (join k1.ind p) Low. From k1.ind ≤ k2.ind and p ≤ q: join k1.ind p ≤ join k2.ind q ≤ Low ✓ (needs join monotonicity lemma). Then structural: evaluations to inl/inr with payloads R T1/T2 and bounds security_le k' k1. For the goal at U: need payloads R U1/U2 (IH on subtype T1 U1 with flows Low Low: R2 T1 Low → R2 U1 Low ✓) and bounds security_le k' k2 (from k' ≤ k1 ≤ k2 ✓).
- S_Prod: similar.
- S_Arrow T1 T2 U1 U2 k1 k2 (subtype U1 T1, subtype T2 U2, security_le k1 k2):
  Goal R2 (Arrow T1 T2 k1) p → R2 (Arrow U1 U2 k2) q. Unfold: obs_q → forall a1 a2 r, flows_to (join k2.reader q) r → R2 U1 Low a1 a2 → R2 U2 (join q k2.ind) (app t1 a1 r) (app t2 a2 r).
  From hypothesis (at p): obs_p ✓ (from obs_q and monotonicity), flows_to (join k1.reader p) r (from join monotonicity and transitivity ✓), R2 T1 Low a1 a2 (from R2 U1 Low a1 a2 via IH on subtype U1 T1 with flows Low Low ✓).
  → R2 T2 (join p k1.ind) (apps). Then need R2 U2 (join q k2.ind) (apps) via IH on subtype T2 U2 with flows_to (join p k1.ind) (join q k2.ind) ✓ (monotonicity of join).
- S_Trans T U V: IH1: R2 T ⊆ R2 U (for flows p q); IH2: R2 U ⊆ R2 V. Compose ✓.

So R2_mono is provable. Note: the IH is used at *subderivations*, so the induction is on the subtype derivation, and the statement is general in p,q. 

But hmm, there's a subtlety: the IH statement must be exactly "forall p q, flows p q -> R2 T p ⊆ R2 U q" for the subderivation. In the S_Arrow case, we use the IH for subtype U1 T1 at p=q=Low ✓ and for subtype T2 U2 at p=join p k1.ind, q=join q k2.ind ✓. Good.

Do we need wf_security anywhere? The subtype rules require wf premises but our monotonicity statement doesn't use them. Fine.

Now the fundamental theorem statement:

```
Lemma fundamental : forall Gamma t T, has_type Gamma t T ->
  forall σ1 σ2, env_rel Gamma σ1 σ2 ->
    R T (subst_env σ1 t) (subst_env σ2 t).
```
where R T := R2 T Low.

```coq
Fixpoint R2 (T : ty) (p : label) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  lc_at 0 t1 /\ lc_at 0 t2 /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      (obs_at p k ->
       forall v1 v2, multi t1 v1 -> multi t2 v2 -> value v1 -> value v2 ->
         (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inl w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl w2 k2 /\
             security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R2 T1 Low w1 w2) \/
         (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inr w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr w2 k2 /\
             security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R2 T2 Low w1 w2))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      (obs_at p k ->
       forall v1 v2, multi t1 v1 -> multi t2 v2 -> value v1 -> value v2 ->
         exists k1 k2 a1 b1 a2 b2,
           v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
           security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R2 T1 Low a1 a2 /\ R2 T2 Low b1 b2)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      (obs_at p k ->
       forall a1 a2 r, flows_to (join p k.(reader)) r -> R2 T1 Low a1 a2 ->
         R2 T2 (join p k.(indirect_reader)) (tm_app t1 a1 r) (tm_app t2 a2 r))
  end.

Fixpoint interp (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit l1 =>
      fun v1 v2 => exists l1 l2, v1 = tm_unit l1 /\ v2 = tm_unit l2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 =>
      fun v1 v2 =>
        (exists v1' v2', v1 = tm_inl v1' /\ v2 = tm_inl v2' /\ interp T1 v1' v2')
        \/ (exists v1' v2', v1 = tm_inr v1' /\ v2 = tm_inr v2' /\ interp T2 v1' v2')
  ...

Key design decision: the relation should be *defined by recursion on ty* and be closed under the operations that typing allows. The final result type is ground, so we need the relation at ground types to imply erased equality (given transparency). The intermediate types include arrows.

Let me propose:

```
Fixpoint interp_val (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit kappa => True   (* all units, erased equal anyway *)
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa =>
      (kappa.(indirect_reader) = High)  (* all values related *)
      \/
      (exists l1 l2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inl w1 l1 /\ v2 = tm_inl w2 l2 /\ interp_val T1 w1 w2)
      \/ (exists ... inr ...)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 kappa =>
      (kappa.(indirect_reader) = High)
      \/ (exists k1 k2 w1 w2 x1 x2, v1 = tm_pair w1 x1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair w2 x2 k2 /\ interp_val T1 w1 w2 /\ interp_val T2 x1 x2)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 kappa =>
      (kappa.(indirect_reader) = High)
      \/ (forall r w1 w2, flows_to kappa.reader r -> interp_val T1 w1 w2 -> interp (ty_protect kappa.indirect_reader T2) (tm_app v1 w1 r) (tm_app v2 w2 r))
  end
```

Hmm wait, but this "if high-indirect then True" makes the relation at low-indirect types require same constructor and related payloads, where payload relation is at T1 regardless of T1's indirect. If T1 is high-indirect, payloads arbitrary, so erased values of the sum could differ (inl(w) vs inl(w') with w,w' arbitrary). Then at a low-indirect sum containing a high-indirect payload, the relation does NOT imply erased equality. At T_result transparent, though, payloads are low-indirect, so erased equality follows by induction over the transparent structure. Good.

But there's a serious problem: the relation at a low-indirect arrow with high-indirect... hmm no.

  end

  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> VR_aux T kappa v1 v2.

Definition env_rel (Gamma : context) (γ1 γ2 : atom -> tm) : Prop :=

Commutation lemma (needed in T_Abs/T_Case):
```
Lemma subst_env_open : forall γ x w body,
  (forall y, lc_at 0 (γ y)) ->
  lc_at 0 w ->
  x ∉ fv body ->
  subst_env (extend γ x w) (open body (tm_fvar x)) = open (subst_env γ body) w.
```
Wait, I earlier showed the equation with γ' on the RHS too:
```
subst_env γ' (open body (fvar x)) = open (subst_env γ' body) w, where γ' = extend γ x w
```
and then if x ∉ fv body, subst_env γ' body = subst_env γ body.

Hmm, is the first equation true without x ∉ fv body? Let's recheck the fvar base case: LHS = γ' y, RHS = open_rec 0 w (γ' y). Since lc (γ' y), open_rec leaves it ✓. But wait: the RHS `open (subst_env γ' body) w = open_rec 0 w (subst_env γ' body)`, and in the fvar y case, subst_env γ' (fvar y) = γ' y, so RHS = open_rec 0 w (γ' y) = γ' y ✓. And LHS = subst_env γ' (fvar y) = γ' y ✓ (open_rec 0 (fvar x) (fvar y) = fvar y since open_rec only changes bvars). Yes! Because open doesn't touch fvars at all. So the first equation holds for all bodies, with lc of γ' values.

Under a binder, the induction needs the equation at level k with extend... but the γ' is the same; the induction statement is:
`forall k body, subst_env γ' (open_rec k (fvar x) body) = open_rec k (γ' x) (subst_env γ' body)` given all γ' y are lc.
Check the bvar case: LHS = subst_env γ' (if k = i then fvar x else bvar i) = if k=i then γ' x else bvar i. RHS = open_rec k (γ' x) (bvar i) = if k=i then γ' x else bvar i ✓.
fvar: LHS = γ' y; RHS = open_rec k (γ' x) (γ' y) = γ' y if lc_at k (γ' y). Need lc_at 0 (γ' y) -> lc_at k (γ' y) ✓ via monotonicity.
Binder: LHS = subst_env γ' (open_rec (S k) (fvar x) b) = IH at S k with same γ' ✓. RHS = open_rec (S k) (γ' x) (subst_env γ' b) ✓.

Definition draft:

```
Definition sec_of_tm (v : tm) : security :=
  match v with
  | tm_unit k | tm_abs _ _ k | tm_pair _ _ k | tm_inl _ k | tm_inr _ k => k
  | _ => public
  end.

Fixpoint VR (T : ty) (kappa : security) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  security_le (sec_of_tm v1) kappa /\
  security_le (sec_of_tm v2) kappa /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      kappa.(indirect_reader) = High \/
      (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inl w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl w2 k2 /\ VR T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2) \/
      (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inr w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr w2 k2 /\ VR T2 (security_of T2) w1 w2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      kappa.(indirect_reader) = High \/
      (exists k1 k2 w1 w2 x1 x2, v1 = tm_pair w1 x1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair w2 x2 k2 /\
          VR T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2 /\ VR T2 (security_of T2) x1 x2)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      kappa.(indirect_reader) = High \/
      (forall r w1 w2, value w1 -> value w2 -> flows_to kappa.(reader) r ->
          VR T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2 ->
          forall u1 u2, evaluates (tm_app v1 w1 r) u1 -> evaluates (tm_app v2 w2 r) u2 ->
            VR T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) kappa.(indirect_reader)) u1 u2)
  end.
```

Fixpoint subst_env (γ : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => γ x
  | tm_unit k => tm_unit k

  ...
  end.
```
Same structure as subst but replacing all fvars.

Actually, before writing, let me settle the design of `subst_env` and its lemmas with exact statements:

```coq
Definition env := atom -> tm.

Definition upd (x : atom) (u : tm) : env :=
  fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then u else tm_fvar y.

Definition extend (gamma : env) (x : atom) (u : tm) : env :=
  fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then u else gamma y.

Fixpoint subst_env (gamma : env) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => gamma x
  | tm_unit k => tm_unit k
  | tm_abs T body k => tm_abs T (subst_env gamma body) k
  | tm_app t1 t2 r => tm_app (subst_env gamma t1) (subst_env gamma t2) r
  | tm_pair t1 t2 k => tm_pair (subst_env gamma t1) (subst_env gamma t2) k
  | tm_fst t r => tm_fst (subst_env gamma t) r
  | tm_snd t r => tm_snd (subst_env gamma t) r
  | tm_inl t k => tm_inl (subst_env gamma t) k
  | tm_inr t k => tm_inr (subst_env gamma t) k
  | tm_case t b1 b2 r => tm_case (subst_env gamma t) (subst_env gamma b1) (subst_env gamma b2) r
  | tm_protect l t => tm_protect l (subst_env gamma t)
  | tm_if c y n r => tm_if (subst_env gamma c) (subst_env gamma y) (subst_env gamma n) r
  end.
```

Lemmas:
1. `subst_env_id : forall t, subst_env (fun y => tm_fvar y) t = t` — by induction on t. 
2. `subst_env_lc : forall k gamma t, (forall y, lc_at 0 (gamma y)) -> lc_at k t -> lc_at k (subst_env gamma t)`.
   Induction on t generalizing k; binder case apply IH at S k; fvar case: gamma y lc at 0 → lc at k by mono.
3. `open_rec_subst_env : forall k gamma x body, (forall y, lc_at 0 (gamma y)) ->
     subst_env gamma (open_rec k (tm_fvar x) body) = open_rec k (gamma x) (subst_env gamma body)`.
   Induction on body generalizing k.
4. `subst_env_extend_fresh : forall gamma x u t, ~ In x (fv t) -> subst_env (extend gamma x u) t = subst_env gamma t`.
   Induction on t. fvar y: if y = x then In x (fv (fvar y)) = In x [y] contradiction; else eqb y x = false. Need to show `if Nat.eqb y x then u else gamma y = gamma y`, from y ≠ x ✓.
5. `subst_env_upd_id : forall x u s, ~ In x (fv s) -> subst_env (upd x u) s = s`.
   Induction on s; fvar y: y ≠ x → upd x u y = fvar y ✓. Others: subst_env of unit etc. = itself ✓. Note: for a compound term s with no x in fv, the subterms also have no x ✓ (fv s = concatenation). Need inversion on In in app: `In x (fv s1 ++ fv s2) -> In x (fv s1) \/ In x (fv s2)` via `in_app_or`. For the single-subterm cases, fv = fv sub ✓ (simpl). For abs: fv (abs T body k) = fv body ✓.

Let me now write VR and IR:

```coq
Fixpoint VR (T : ty) (kappa : security) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  flows_to (sec_of_tm v1).(indirect_reader) kappa.(indirect_reader) /\
  flows_to (sec_of_tm v2).(indirect_reader) kappa.(indirect_reader) /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      kappa.(indirect_reader) = High \/
      (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inl w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl w2 k2 /\
         VR T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2) \/
      (exists k1 k2 w1 w2, v1 = tm_inr w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr w2 k2 /\
         VR T2 (security_of T2) w1 w2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      kappa.(indirect_reader) = High \/
      (exists k1 k2 w1 w2 x1 x2, v1 = tm_pair w1 x1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair w2 x2 k2 /\
         VR T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2 /\ VR T2 (security_of T2) x1 x2)
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      kappa.(indirect_reader) = High \/
      (forall r w1 w2, value w1 -> value w2 -> flows_to kappa.(reader) r ->
         VR T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2 ->
         forall u1 u2, evaluates (tm_app v1 w1 r) u1 -> evaluates (tm_app v2 w2 r) u2 ->
           VR T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) kappa.(indirect_reader)) u1 u2)
  end.

Definition IR (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> VR T (security_of T) v1 v2.
```

Guard checker: recursive calls on T1/T2 strict subterms ✓. But hmm, the arrow branch has `VR T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) kappa.(indirect_reader)) u1 u2` where T2 is a subterm ✓.

Potential issue: the recursive occurrences under the `match T with` need the match to be on T (the first argument) ✓.

```
Lemma VR_sum_inl : forall T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2,
  kappa.(indirect_reader) = Low ->
  VR (Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa) kappa (tm_inl w1 ka1) (tm_inl w2 ka2) ->
  VR T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2.
Proof.
  intros T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2 Hlow HVR.
  destruct (VR_sum_low T1 T2 kappa (tm_inl w1 ka1) (tm_inl w2 ka2) Hlow HVR) as [H | H].
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]].
    injection E1 as Ev1 _. injection E2 as Ev2 _. subst v1. subst v2. exact HR.
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]]. discriminate E1.
Qed.

Lemma VR_sum_inr : forall T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2,
  kappa.(indirect_reader) = Low ->
  VR (Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa) kappa (tm_inr w1 ka1) (tm_inr w2 ka2) ->
  VR T2 (security_of T2) w1 w2.
Proof.
  intros T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2 Hlow HVR.
  destruct (VR_sum_low T1 T2 kappa (tm_inr w1 ka1) (tm_inr w2 ka2) Hlow HVR) as [H | H].
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]]. discriminate E1.
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]].
    injection E1 as Ev1 _. injection E2 as Ev2 _. subst v1. subst v2. exact HR.
Qed.

Lemma VR_sum_mismatch_lr : forall T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2,
  kappa.(indirect_reader) = Low ->
  VR (Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa) kappa (tm_inl w1 ka1) (tm_inr w2 ka2) -> False.
Proof.
  intros ... HVR. destruct (VR_sum_low ...) as [H|H];
  destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]]; discriminate E1.
Qed.

Lemma VR_sum_mismatch_rl : ... (tm_inr ...) (tm_inl ...) -> False.
```

```coq
Lemma VR_sum_inl : forall T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2,
  kappa.(indirect_reader) = Low ->
  VR (Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa) kappa (tm_inl w1 ka1) (tm_inl w2 ka2) ->
  VR T1 (security_of T1) w1 w2.
Proof.
  intros T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2 Hlow HVR.
  destruct (VR_sum_low T1 T2 kappa (tm_inl w1 ka1) (tm_inl w2 ka2) Hlow HVR) as [H | H].
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]].
    injection E1 as Ev1 _. injection E2 as Ev2 _. subst v1. subst v2. exact HR.
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]]. discriminate E1.
Qed.

Lemma VR_sum_inr : forall T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2,
  kappa.(indirect_reader) = Low ->
  VR (Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa) kappa (tm_inr w1 ka1) (tm_inr w2 ka2) ->
  VR T2 (security_of T2) w1 w2.
Proof.
  intros T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2 Hlow HVR.
  destruct (VR_sum_low T1 T2 kappa (tm_inr w1 ka1) (tm_inr w2 ka2) Hlow HVR) as [H | H].
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]]. discriminate E1.
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]].
    injection E1 as Ev1 _. injection E2 as Ev2 _. subst v1. subst v2. exact HR.
Qed.

Lemma VR_sum_mismatch_lr : forall T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2,
  kappa.(indirect_reader) = Low ->
  VR (Ty_Sum T1 T2 kappa) kappa (tm_inl w1 ka1) (tm_inr w2 ka2) -> False.
Proof.
  intros T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2 Hlow HVR.
  destruct (VR_sum_low T1 T2 kappa (tm_inl w1 ka1) (tm_inr w2 ka2) Hlow HVR) as [H | H].
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]]. discriminate E2.
  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]]. discriminate E1.
Qed.

Lemma VR_sum_mismatch_rl : forall T1 T2 kappa w1 w2 ka1 ka2,

  - destruct H as [k1 [k2 [v1 [v2 [E1 [E2 HR]]]]]]. discriminate E2.
Qed.

  forall gamma1 gamma2, env_rel Gamma gamma1 gamma2 ->
  IR T (subst_env gamma1 t) (subst_env gamma2 t).
Proof.
  intros Gamma t T H.
  induction H as
    [ Gamma x T Hlook Hwf
    | Gamma kappa Hwf
    | L Gamma T1 body T2 kappa HwfT1 Hwfkap Hbody IHbody
    | Gamma t1 t2 T1 T2 kappa r H1 IH1 H2 IH2 Hflow
    | Gamma t1 t2 T1 T2 kappa H1 IH1 H2 IH2 Hwf

    | Gamma t T1 T2 kappa r H1 IH1 Hflow
    | Gamma t T1 T2 kappa H1 IH1 HwfT2 Hwfkap
    | Gamma t T1 T2 kappa HwfT1 H1 IH1 Hwfkap
    | L Gamma t body1 body2 T1 T2 T kappa r H1 IH1 Hflow Hb1 IHb1 Hb2 IHb2
    | Gamma t T l H1 IH1
    | Gamma t T U H1 IH1 Hsub
    | Gamma c yes no k T r H1 IH1 H2 IH2 H3 IH3 Hflow ];
  intros gamma1 gamma2 Henv; simpl.
